top_story.headline: President Donald J. Trump files a 517-transaction trade report
top_story.dek: A new periodic transaction report lists hundreds of purchases and sales, with parsed values in the tens of millions of dollars.
paragraphs: President Donald J. Trump filed a periodic transaction report posted by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics on October 8, 2026, listing 517 transactions.

An automated parse of the scanned PDF read 480 of the 517 line items: 247 purchases and 213 sales, with 20 unclear from the scan. The disclosed ranges for the parsed trades total roughly $65 million to $230 million, and about 55 look like municipal or other bonds. The scan's transaction-date text is partly garbled, so the reporting period isn't stated here. See the Trump trades section below for the sector breakdown.

sections.headline: New appointees file ethics certifications as two officials complete required divestitures
paragraphs: The White House Office and the National Credit Union Administration received ethics documents from senior officials on October 8, while the Departments of Justice and State confirmed divestiture certificates for appointees. The Department of Agriculture's newly confirmed Under Secretary for Trade & Foreign Agricultural Affairs filed both an ethics agreement and a routine financial disclosure request.

items: • Leslie Wulff at the Department of Justice filed a Certificate of Divestiture (OGE-2026-160); only the fact of the divestiture is confirmed, not the asset.
• Eric Wendt at the Department of State filed a Certificate of Divestiture (OGE-2026-161); only the fact of the divestiture is confirmed, not the asset.

• Donald J Trump, President of the United States at the White House Office, filed a 278 Transaction Report disclosing periodic purchases of municipal bonds and corporate securities throughout August 2026, including positions in infrastructure and utility bonds across multiple states, and equity purchases in financial services and technology firms.

• John Crews, Member of the National Credit Union Administration Board, filed a Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance certifying that he completed all required resignations and divestitures within the timeframes specified in his ethics agreement, with a confirmation date of August 7, 2026.

• Gregory A Ibach, Under Secretary for Trade & Foreign Agricultural Affairs at the Department of Agriculture, filed an Ethics Agreement committing to resign from his position with the Aksarben Foundation upon confirmation, maintain his trustee position in Family Trust #1 without compensation, cease consulting services, retain passive investment income from GTI Inc., maintain fixed-rate farmland leases, and recuse from matters involving his spouse's employer.
• Gregory A Ibach — Nominee 278 (Request this Document), Department of Agriculture.

sections.headline: No new or terminated foreign-agent registrants
paragraphs: The Department of Justice's FARA e-file reports for October 7 through October 8, 2026 show zero new registrants and zero terminated registrants (new; terminated).

sections.headline: Three new Senate filings; one is a stock-trade report with no stock trades
paragraphs: Three Senate filings were new since the last edition, and all three were read in full. Sen. John Fetterman's periodic transaction report covers only corporate bond purchases by a dependent child, so there is no equity table. No House filings were new today: the three House filings in the window (a candidate report from Te Brown and trade reports from Rep. Lloyd Doggett and Rep. Vince Fong) were already covered in earlier editions. The 30-filing read cap was not reached.

items: Sen. John Fetterman (Democrat, Pennsylvania) filed a periodic transaction report on October 7, 2026 with two transactions, both owned by a dependent child: purchases of Dell International LLC/EMC Corporation corporate bonds (5.6% coupon, maturing September 15, 2033) on September 15 and September 16, 2026, each valued at $1,001 - $15,000. Neither involves a publicly traded stock ticker.

Sen. Tim Scott (Republican, South Carolina) filed Amendment 1 to his Calendar 2025 annual report on October 6, 2026. It lists $94,563 in royalties from HarperCollins Publishing LLC, a $4,685 South Carolina retirement payment, spousal wages from MEB LLC, and a 50% interest in Rivertown Investments, LLC, a residential real-estate company holding three South Carolina rental properties valued at $100,001 - $250,000 each, alongside bank, life-insurance and mutual-fund holdings.

Justin Murphy, a New Jersey Senate candidate, filed a candidate report on October 7, 2026 (candidacy commenced January 15, 2026). It reports $28,500 in self-employment income as a solo-practitioner attorney, no reportable assets, and a $100,001 - $250,000 law-school student loan from Navient and Nelnet.

blocks.text: Tracking 483 Senate-confirmed officials with ethics agreements since Jan. 20, 2025. Deadlines are counted from the confirmation date on congress.gov plus the agreement's stated window (usually 90 days) -- OGE can grant extensions that aren't public, so treat each flag as a lead to confirm, not a finding. OGE posts certifications with a lag, so nothing inside 30 days of a deadline is flagged. A certification filed but not yet posted by OGE will read as missing: confirm with the agency before publishing.

sections.headline: Donald J. Trump reported 517 personal trades
paragraphs: President Donald J. Trump filed a periodic transaction report (posted 10/8/2026) listing 517 transactions made between 8/3/2026 and 8/17/7026.
